claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a random, homogeneous solid solution.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce partial atomic ordering in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce segregation, such as Pt/Pd-rich regions, in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Changes in local atomic ordering modify the catalyst's electronic structure.
Reordering produces local variations in electronic properties.
Local electronic variations alter the adsorption energy of ethanol.
Local electronic variations alter the adsorption energies of ethanol oxidation intermediates.
The adsorption-energy changes enhance ethanol oxidation kinetics.
Annealing-induced atomic ordering will increase ethanol oxidation current density relative to an unannealed random-alloy baseline.
Annealing-induced atomic ordering will lower ethanol oxidation overpotential relative to an unannealed random-alloy baseline.
The proposed ordering effect is expected to hold for alkaline ethanol oxidation at 60–80 °C.
At other pH values, temperatures, or reaction media, factors other than local ordering may dominate catalytic behavior.
No direct eligible evidence is available for controlled-ordering effects in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs under ethanol oxidation conditions.
The experiment compares an unannealed random-solid-solution control with a thermally annealed sample under otherwise identical ethanol oxidation conditions.
A lack of statistically significant activity or overpotential improvement in an annealed sample is proposed as a falsifying result.
Failure to detect a meaningful ordering change after annealing is proposed as a falsifying result.
